title: Early believers were moved by the Word's luminous power, not by Church authority or the preachers' fame
pass_a_gloss: 3. Here it is asked what moved these and other barbarians whom the Apostles taught, that they preferred to die rather than deny the faith. 4. They did not believe moved by those human arguments, because these produce only human faith; nor by the authority of the Church, because it was then unknown to them, and if proved the proof would have to be taken from the scriptures themselves and so the demonstration would be circular; nor by the authority of those who preached, who were unarmed fishermen and obscure weavers. Therefore they believed moved by the luminous virtue and spiritual efficacy of the word itself. 5. No effect which depends through itself from some cause can exist without that cause. But that solid assent is sometimes without the known authority of the Church. Therefore this assent does not depend from the authority of the Church as from a cause through itself. 6. Bellarmine confesses: there is no persuasion which can compel a man to believe supernatural articles unless the mind is divinely helped.
pass_b_english: What moved the "barbarians" the Apostles taught to prefer death to deserting the faith? Not the human arguments (they produce only human faith); not the Church's authority (then unknown to them — and if proved from Scripture, circular); not the preachers' authority (unarmed fishermen and obscure weavers). Therefore they believed moved by the luminous power and spiritual efficacy of the Word itself, handed down to us through Scripture.

No effect that depends of itself on a cause can exist without that cause. But solid assent to Scripture sometimes exists without the Church's known authority. Therefore this assent does not depend on the Church's authority as on a cause of itself — as history shows of those who believed from New Testament reading alone. Bellarmine himself confesses: no persuasion can compel belief in supernatural articles unless the mind is divinely helped — not even miracles entirely convince.
source_text: Barbari Apostolorum non Ecclesiae authoritate (tunc incognita; circularis), nec praedicatorum (piscatores), sed luminosa virtute verbi crediderunt. Assensus solidus aliquando sine cognita Ecclesiae authoritate; ergo non ab ea ut a causa per se. Bellarminus: nulla persuasio cogit ad articulos supernaturales nisi mens divinitus adjuvetur.
